title: Does Your Generalist Skill Optimizer Really Incentivize Agentic Tasks? Rethinking Skill Optimization via Bipartite Attribution
why: Audit of generalist skill optimizers (GEPA, SkillOpt, SkillAdam): BiPA replays acceptance rules on seed-identical candidates and attributes token cost via bipartite turn–context graphs. Reports near-zero test gains vs seed and ~16% more input tokens; proposes accept/charge/delete design principles for skill/playbook learning loops.
mechanism: Measurement/audit layer for skill-library optimizers: selection-only baseline for acceptance gates; bipartite attribution of extra turns/tokens to added skill rules (non-weight context edits).
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: three optimizers × three agentic benchmarks × two models; learned skills ~0.1 points above handwritten seed on test; dev gains vanish under selection-alone replay; ~16% more input tokens via extra turns.
